mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when this trigger is met (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when INDPRO declines for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer savings (RSAFS) by more than 5% month-over-month indicate tighter monetary policy and reduced household liquidity, which together depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND RSAFS falls > 5% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS rises and RSAFS falls > 5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both housing starts (HOUST) and personal income (implied by PAYEMS) above their 12-month moving averages signals strengthening demand fundamentals, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and PAYEMS exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annual increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which increases the likelihood of aggressive central bank tightening and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL YoY > 3% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero during periods of sustained CPIAUCSL > 3% YoY for six months.
